procedures.body:
# Group alternatives under the mandatory boolean condition

## When to apply
When a boolean filter requires mandatory condition A and at least one positive alternative B or C. All boolean values have already been computed correctly. When an explicit mode negates the alternatives, apply the negation to the complete grouped alternatives while preserving A.

## Procedure
1. Group the alternatives as (B OR C).
2. In positive mode, combine the group with the mandatory condition as A AND (B OR C).
3. In explicitly negated mode, combine the mandatory condition with the negated group as A AND NOT (B OR C).
4. Verify that A=false produces false regardless of the values of B and C.

## Pitfalls
Do not emit A AND B OR C without grouping. Do not negate only B or change the meaning of the already computed input values. Do not drop the mandatory condition.

# Convert one-based selection positions to zero-based indices

## When to apply
When a user selects one-based position p in a one-dimensional list of length N, and the interface and target collection use the same element ordering.

## Procedure
1. Validate that 1 <= p <= N; reject an invalid position explicitly.
2. Subtract one exactly once and access index p-1.
3. The first position maps to index 0 and the last position maps to N-1.

## Pitfalls
Do not use a one-based position directly as an index or subtract one twice. This arithmetic assumes the interface and target collection have the same ordering.

event.observed: In positive mode, a record with A=false, B=true and C=true incorrectly passes the generated A AND B OR C expression.
event.outcome: Using A AND (B OR C) makes the record fail as required while preserving the positive alternatives.

# Group alternatives under the mandatory boolean condition

## When to apply
When a boolean filter requires mandatory condition A and at least one positive alternative B or C. All boolean values have already been computed correctly.

## Procedure
1. Group the alternatives as (B OR C).
2. Combine the group with the mandatory condition as A AND (B OR C).
3. Verify that A=false produces false regardless of the values of B and C.

## Pitfalls
Do not emit A AND B OR C without grouping. Do not drop the mandatory condition or change the meaning of the already computed input values.

# Convert one-based selection positions to zero-based indices

## When to apply
When a user selects a one-based position p in a one-dimensional list of length N, or one-based row r and column c in a grid, and the interface and target collection use the same element ordering.

## Procedure
1. For a one-dimensional list, validate that 1 <= p <= N; reject an invalid position explicitly.
2. For a grid, validate row and column bounds independently against their respective dimensions; reject an invalid coordinate explicitly.
3. Subtract one exactly once from each supplied position or coordinate, then access index p-1 for a list or grid[r-1][c-1] for a grid.
4. The first position maps to index 0 and the last position maps to N-1; for a grid, the first row and column map to index 0 in their respective dimensions.

## Pitfalls
Do not use a one-based position directly as an index or subtract one twice. For grids, do not convert only one coordinate. This arithmetic assumes the interface and target collection have the same ordering.

event.observed: In the one-dimensional list [A, B, C, D], displayed and stored in the same order, the last position 4 was used directly as index 4 and was outside the collection.
event.outcome: Validating the position and converting 4-1=3 returned D; the position was converted only once.
